nodes.label: Trustee Duties, Powers and Liabilities
nodes.summary: Trustee duties: Hastings-Bass rule, anti-Bartlett clauses, exemption clauses, substratum rule, and core duties of investment, impartiality, and accounting.

nodes.label: Duty to Consider (The Rule in Hastings-Bass)
nodes.summary: A trustee must take into account all relevant considerations when exercising a discretionary power. If a trustee fails to do so, the exercise may be set aside. However, Pitt v Holt restricted this: a breach of duty must be shown; flawed professional advice alone is insufficient.

nodes.label: Equitable Rescission for Mistake
nodes.summary: Even if Hastings-Bass does not apply, a trustee's decision may be set aside for mistake if the mistake is sufficiently grave and it would be unconscionable to leave the transaction uncorrected.

nodes.label: Anti-Bartlett Clauses and Supervisory Duties
nodes.summary: Trust deeds may exclude the trustee's duty to supervise or intervene in the business of an underlying company. CFA in Zhang Hong Li affirmed that anti-Bartlett provisions are effective; trustees have no residual high-level supervisory duty if the deed excludes it.

nodes.label: Trust Exemption Clauses
nodes.summary: Exemption clauses can relieve trustees from liability for negligence or even gross negligence, but cannot exclude liability for actual fraud or wilful default. The Trustee Ordinance Cap 29 s.41W provides a statutory duty of care for professional trustees.

nodes.label: The Substratum Rule (Power of Amendment)
nodes.summary: A power of amendment cannot be exercised to destroy the fundamental purpose (substratum) of the trust, even if the power is widely drafted. PC struck down amendment that fundamentally changed the family trust's substratum.

nodes.label: Duty to Invest
nodes.summary: Trustees must invest trust funds in accordance with the Trustee Ordinance and the trust instrument. The standard is that of a prudent person of business acting in the best interests of the beneficiaries.

nodes.label: Duty to Act Impartially
nodes.summary: Trustees must act impartially between different classes of beneficiaries, e.g. life tenants and remaindermen. Investment decisions must balance income and capital growth appropriately.

nodes.label: Duty to Account and Provide Information
nodes.summary: Trustees must keep proper accounts and records, and provide beneficiaries with information about the trust. The duty is subject to the trustee's discretion and the nature of the beneficiary's interest.

nodes.label: Powers of Maintenance and Advancement
nodes.summary: Trustees may have powers to apply income or capital for the benefit of a beneficiary before they become absolutely entitled. Statutory powers under the Trustee Ordinance Cap 29, subject to the trust instrument.

nodes.label: Duty to Pay the Right Person
nodes.summary: Trustees are strictly liable for distribution to the wrong beneficiary. Proper diligence in identifying beneficiaries and complying with the trust terms is essential.

nodes.label: Pitt v Holt / Futter v Futter [2013] UKSC 26
nodes.summary: Hastings-Bass restricted: a decision is voidable only if the trustee failed to consider a relevant matter and that failure was not due to the trustee's own fault. Also: equitable rescission for grave mistake.

nodes.label: Zhang Hong Li v DBS Bank (Hong Kong) Ltd [2019] 3 HKLRD 650 (CFA)
nodes.summary: Anti-Bartlett clause: CFA affirmed anti-Bartlett provisions are effective; trustees have no residual high-level supervisory duty if deed excludes such duty.

nodes.label: Armitage v Nurse [1998] Ch 241 (CA)
nodes.summary: Exemption clauses: validly excluded liability for negligence; only fraud cannot be excluded. PC affirmed in Spread Trustee.

nodes.label: Spread Trustee Co Ltd v Hutcheson [2011] UKPC 13
nodes.summary: Exemption clauses: PC affirmed Armitage v Nurse. Exemption clauses valid for negligence; fraud exception stands.

nodes.label: Grand View Private Trust Co v Wong [2022] UKPC 47
nodes.summary: Substratum rule: PC struck down trustee's use of amendment power to add charitable foundation and exclude family beneficiaries, as it fundamentally changed the substratum of the family trust.

nodes.label: Verify HK Trustee Duty Leading Cases
nodes.summary: Research HK applications of Pitt v Holt, anti-Bartlett cases, exemption clause limits under Cap 29 s.41W, and any HK cases on the substratum rule.
